title: Frozen claim
description: The thing everything else binds to. A domain pack extends this with its own frozen content — anything that, if it changed silently, would make a result stop meaning what it claimed to mean. REQUIRED covers what an AUTHOR supplies. `status` and `payload_sha256` are machinery: a claim gets its status from the reducer and its seal when it becomes a transmitted packet, so requiring an author to write either produces guesses — and a guess that happens to match is indistinguishable from knowledge. This was decided by evidence rather than taste: a real claim from a campaign that reached VERIFIED could not satisfy this schema, and when every implementer including the fixture diverges the same way, the specification is what is wrong.

lineage_of.description: The claim this was derived from. Hash-linked, not id-linked: an id is mutable, so without from/to hashes you cannot verify a claim actually descends from the ancestor it names — which is exactly how target drift launders itself.

exact_statement.description: The claim as stated, with quantifier order explicit. No paraphrase.

definitions.description: Every non-standard term used in exact_statement.

objective.description: What establishing this claim is for. Distinguishes a target from a step toward one.

success_condition.description: Exactly what would count as establishing this. Stated before work begins.

failure_condition.description: Exactly what would count as refuting it. A claim with no stated failure condition is not falsifiable and cannot be frozen.

frozen_conditions.description: Domain-supplied content that must not drift: inputs, versions, environments, tolerances, baselines, populations. The pack's claim schema names the required keys.

allowed_mutations.description: Mutations pre-authorized without opening a new lineage. Each records the axis changed and why.

target_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonical form of this claim. Must agree across work item, artifact, adapter input, receipt, and result.

status.description: See references/status_vocabulary.md. A frozen claim starts OPEN or CONJECTURE; only admission moves it. Added by the machinery, not by the author; optional here for that reason and required of the packet once it is transmitted.

source_status.description: What is already known about this claim externally, and how well checked that is.

retrieved.description: False means nobody opened it. A pointer is not a source: without retrieved content, date_checked is a field that was filled in, not a check that was run.

locator.description: Exact position inside the document that the claim rests on.

excerpt.description: The quoted span supporting the claim.

sources_sha256.description: Hash over the canonical sources array. Pins the set as of the moment it was audited, so sources cannot be appended — or a contradicting one dropped — after a novelty determination.

payload_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of this packet with payload_sha256 removed: sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes. Seals the packet and makes it addressable by later packets — an id alone is a mutable label. Added by the machinery, not by the author; optional here for that reason and required of the packet once it is transmitted.

canonical_fields.description: The exact ordered field list target_sha256 is computed over; a pack appends its frozen fields. Without this, two parties can each compute 'the canonical form' differently — producing either a spurious disqualifying mismatch, or a green hash that silently missed a changed domain field.

dependency_mode.description: How this claim's dependencies combine. AND = all required; OR = any one suffices. Omitting the distinction makes closure-checking wrong rather than merely absent: an AND node with two of three legs open looks identical to a satisfied OR node.
